provenance.locator: Table 1A (Solid Nodules), multiple-nodule row, 6-8 mm and >8 mm columns: after the initial CT at 3-6 months, the subsequent CT at 18-24 months is recommended for high risk. Recommendation 2: multiple solid noncalcified nodules, at least one >=6 mm, followed by a second scan at 18-24 months depending on estimated risk. Only this second CT is governed; later surveillance is not executed. Recommendation 2's contextual notes on known or suspected primary neoplasm and active infection are not executable conditions here. Paraphrase only.

provenance.locator: Risk Estimation and Risk Models: low risk is estimated cancer risk <5%; high risk combines ACCP intermediate (5-65%) and high (>65%) categories. Relevant factors include age, smoking exposure, nodule size, margin morphology, and upper-lobe location. No deterministic calculator is implemented; the category is clinician-attested per #16 comments 5917098959, 5917117015 and 6338095264 (2.4).

provenance.locator: Recommendation 2: management may be guided by a larger or more suspicious (dominant) nodule according to the solitary-nodule recommendations; the dominant nodule is not necessarily the largest. Paraphrase only. Represented solely as the clinician's fresh, current-assessment confirmation fleischner_multiple_solid_no_individual_nodule_requires_solitary_management (Candidate-C HITL 3/4; Candidate-D sign-off D2). Non-confirmation is outside current scope, with no substitute and no redirect. No lesion is identified or selected.

recommendation.rationale: Fleischner (2017) Recommendation 2 and Table 1A describe, for multiple solid noncalcified pulmonary nodules found incidentally with at least one nodule 6 mm or larger, an initial CT at 3-6 months followed by a second CT at 18-24 months depending on estimated risk; for a patient at high risk, this CT at 18-24 months is recommended — in a patient >=35 years old with no known malignancy history and not immunocompromised. This rule applies only at the first follow-up of an initial Fleischner multiple solid nodule episode with at least one nodule 6 mm or larger for which CT at 3-6 months was intended, as attested by the clinician. Anchoring the 18-24-month interval to the baseline CT is an approved Clinical/Product interpretation of the source's surveillance sequence, not a verbatim source quotation; this application performs no date calculation. The high-risk category is the clinician's explicit Fleischner risk decision (Fleischner high risk combines the ACCP intermediate- and high-risk categories, estimated cancer risk 5% or above); this application does not calculate, score, weight, or infer it from any other input. This recommendation applies only because the clinician has confirmed at this follow-up that no individual larger or more suspicious nodule currently requires management according to the Fleischner solitary-nodule recommendations, and has not decided that no further routine surveillance is planned. No index, largest, dominant, or most-suspicious nodule is identified, ranked, or selected by this application, and no current stability, persistence, size, or regression criterion is evaluated. Solitary-nodule-directed management of any individual nodule, surveillance after the CT at 18-24 months, PET/CT, biopsy, and resection are outside this Rule-Set Release and must not be inferred from it.
